Marzipan Fruits

Served at: St. Nicholas Day

Makes about 30 small fruitsPrep 30 min

Marzipan fruits are colorful, sweet confections made from almond paste and sugar, shaped and painted to resemble real fruits. They are traditionally served on St. Nicholas Day, celebrated on December 6th in many European countries, symbolizing the festive spirit and the joy of giving.

Ingredients

  • 1 lb (450 g) almond paste
  • 1 cup (120 g) powdered sugar
  • 1-2 tbsp (15-30 ml) water or orange blossom water
  • Food coloring (red, green, yellow, orange, brown)
  • Edible markers or cocoa powder for details

Method

  1. Crumble the almond paste into a mixing bowl.
  2. Add powdered sugar and mix well.
  3. Gradually add water or orange blossom water to form a smooth, pliable dough.
  4. Divide the dough into small portions for each fruit you want to create.
  5. Shape each portion into the desired fruit shape (e.g., apples, pears, oranges, bananas).
  6. Use food coloring to tint each fruit by kneading a small amount of color into the dough or painting the surface with a brush dipped in diluted food coloring.
  7. Add details like stems, leaves, or spots using edible markers or a fine brush with cocoa powder.
  8. Allow the marzipan fruits to dry and firm up at room temperature for several hours before serving.

Tips

  • Use orange blossom water for a traditional floral aroma, or substitute with rose water for a different fragrance.
  • If you don’t have edible markers, use a toothpick dipped in cocoa powder or colored food gel to add details.
  • Store marzipan fruits in an airtight container at room temperature to keep them fresh and soft.
